subject: Dedicated vs Private VPC - data isolation follow-up

Subject: Great chat today — next steps on Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Hi Lydia —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and next steps so we stay aligned on data isolation requirements and deployment options: 

Summary of the ask:
- FinSecure needs strict data isolation for customer PII and transaction logs.
- Primary requirement: no co-mingling of persistent customer data across tenants; control plane access must be restricted to FinSecure.
- Secondary: ability to host in our US regions and integration with your KMS/HSM for key custody.

What we covered:
- Hosted API: fastest to launch but runs on multi-tenant control plane and shared GPUs; not suitable given current isolation needs.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools (single-tenant inference runtime) with logical isolation; good throughput and faster onboarding than Private. Persistent data (logs, caches) still sit in Redwood-managed storage unless you enable Private features.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full customer-managed network and optional on-prem package; control plane can be customer-hosted, and we can integrate KMS/HSM — aligns best with strict isolation requirements.

Attachments I mentioned:
- SOC2 questionnaire (attached) — we’ve filled relevant sections based on the data we discussed.
- Example network diagram stub (attached) showing VPC peering and control plane options.

Next steps (proposed):
1) FinSecure to confirm: Is the requirement to prevent any Redwood-managed persistent storage from containing customer data (yes/no)?
2) If yes, we propose a Private VPC evaluation. We’ll schedule a 45-min deep-dive with Nikhil (solutions) to go through the architecture and KMS integration.
3) If no, Dedicated may suffice — we’ll provide an SLA/commit tier and onboarding checklist.

Would you be available for the technical deep-dive on Thu, Mar 4 at 10am PT? I’ll keep it focused on data flow, key custody, and logging.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Great chat today — next steps on Dedicated vs Private VPC (data isolation)

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

1) Our compliance team requires that customer data (PII and transaction logs) never be written to any third-party managed persistent storage in shared tenancy. That means Redwood-managed S3 buckets or database instances that store FinSecure data are unacceptable unless they are dedicated to FinSecure and under contract.

2) Control plane access: we need audit log evidence that only FinSecure administrators can access environment config and key materials. Ideally, control plane should be in our VPC or under our tenancy with RBAC enforced.

Given the above, it sounds like Private VPC (with customer-managed control plane) is the safest path. That said, timeline is a concern — we’d like to evaluate effort and cost delta vs Dedicated. Can Nikhil run through the architecture and call out what components would still be managed by Redwood in a Dedicated deployment vs fully customer-managed in a Private deployment?

Also, I attached a short questionnaire from our compliance team (see SOC2 doc you sent) — we started annotating a few items.

Thanks,
Lydia Park
Director, Security & Compliance | FinSecure

Hi Lydia —

Thanks for the notes — happy to run through the differences. High-level breakdown below; I’ll cover these in more depth on the technical deep-dive.

Dedicated (Redwood-managed dedicated capacity):
- Inference runtime is single-tenant at the GPU/pool level (your workloads aren’t co-located with other customers on the same GPU instances).
- Control plane and orchestration remain Redwood-managed; we offer strict RBAC and audit logs, and we can contractually restrict support access.
- Persistent artifacts (request logs, metrics, model cache) by default live in Redwood-managed storage. We can offer dedicated buckets/instances for enterprise customers under contract to minimize co-mingling risk — but the control plane still runs in our environment.
- KMS: we can integrate customer KMS for model encryption at rest (customer-managed keys) for certain artifacts; however some platform metadata may still be in our control plane.

Private VPC / On-prem:
- Control plane can be deployed in your VPC or on-prem: full tenant isolation. No Redwood-managed persistent storage unless you opt-in.
- Network: VPC peering or private connectivity; all egress is within your VPC.
- Key management: supports KMS/HSM under your tenancy; you retain keys and we never have access.
- Onboarding and ops: longer lead time (ops coordination, networking, certs), but meets strict compliance requirements.

Decision heuristics we recommend:
- If policy forbids any third-party-managed persistent storage of regulated data: choose Private.
- If you can accept dedicated-but-Redwood-managed storage under contractual guarantees and reduced time-to-value: Dedicated can be a faster, lower-cost path.

For the deep-dive I’ll prepare a short architecture slide (control plane components, data flows, KMS touchpoints) and a checklist of what we need from FinSecure (VPC CIDRs, KMS details, admin list, compliance POA).

Available slots: Thu Mar 4 at 10am PT (Marissa suggested) or Fri Mar 5 at 9am PT. Which works?

Cheers,
